incidents.victim: Global FortiGate device owners (86,644+ devices across 194 countries)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of unpatched FortiGate firewall vulnerabilities to harvest credentials from internet-exposed management interfaces at scale.
incidents.impact: 86,644+ FortiGate devices compromised across 194 countries; stolen credentials actively used as ransomware entry points; IC3/CISA joint advisory issued urging immediate remediation.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Ivanti Connect Secure VPN (multiple sectors)
incidents.vector: Chained zero-day exploit (CVE-2026-104935) combining authentication bypass and RCE; Ivanti discovered the flaw internally in June but did not issue an out-of-band patch before attackers exploited it.
incidents.impact: Limited number of customers confirmed compromised before patch release; post-exploitation included credential theft, Active Directory exfiltration, log tampering, and reconnaissance; CISA warns Ivanti's own Integrity Checker Tool may not detect exploitation.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Windows (all sectors)
incidents.vector: CVE-2026-96951 Windows Shell security feature bypass exploited in the wild; allows attackers to deliver malicious files while bypassing Mark of the Web warnings that would otherwise alert users.
incidents.impact: Microsoft patched a record 1,413 CVEs in a single release; one zero-day actively exploited; critical RCE flaws in Exchange Server (CVE-2026-70571), Windows DHCP Server (10 flaws, 5 critical), and Office also addressed.

incidents.victim: Telecom managed service provider and 500+ downstream customer organizations
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2024-47575 (FortiManager) to breach a telecom MSP, then exfiltrate configurations for 500+ managed FortiGate devices including credentials, network topology, and VPN settings.
incidents.impact: Memory-resident ARM64 PEERSTITCH implant deployed on FortiGate devices; 500+ downstream organizations' firewall credentials and network designs exposed; sophisticated supply-chain-style persistent access enabling follow-on attacks.

incidents.victim: 75,000+ organizations (healthcare, financial services, technology, wholesale distribution)
incidents.vector: YAM Store phishing-as-a-service platform distributed over 1 billion phishing messages to organizations in Japan, US, Australia, and India via branded kits impersonating Microsoft and healthcare portals.
incidents.impact: Microsoft and Health-ISAC disrupted the YAM Store ecosystem via court order; 75,000+ organizations targeted with credential-theft phishing at unprecedented scale; large-scale financial fraud facilitated.

incidents.victim: 395 organizations (440 PaperCut print management instances)
incidents.vector: Coordinated fleet of 100+ AI agents automated the exploitation of CVE-2026-81578/82078 in PaperCut print management software to compromise instances across hundreds of organizations simultaneously.
incidents.impact: 440 PaperCut instances at 395 organizations compromised; credentials harvested; represents first documented large-scale AI-agent-coordinated exploitation campaign by Russia-linked actors.

incidents.victim: 49+ critical infrastructure organizations (energy, utilities, government)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of WordPress and Gitea CVE vulnerabilities for initial access to critical infrastructure networks across multiple countries.
incidents.impact: 49+ critical infrastructure organizations compromised; suspected pre-positioning and intelligence collection across energy, utilities, and government sectors.

incidents.victim: Russian companies (Exchange servers)
incidents.vector: Compromised VPN credentials used for initial access; GhostContainer backdoor deployed on Microsoft Exchange servers at Russian organizations.
incidents.impact: Exchange servers at multiple Russian companies backdoored for persistent access; enables ongoing email surveillance and data exfiltration.

incidents.victim: South Korean financial organizations
incidents.vector: ARTEX campaign uses AI-driven reconnaissance and exploitation tooling to target South Korean financial sector networks.
incidents.impact: Data exfiltrated from South Korean financial institutions; AI-augmented tradecraft accelerates attack cycle and complicates attribution.

incidents.victim: Government organizations across 9 CIS countries
incidents.vector: Multiple infection chains including macro-enabled Office documents and WinRAR exploit targeting government organizations with a specific interest in water and energy sector intelligence.
incidents.impact: Government organizations across Central Asia and former Soviet states compromised; water and energy sector targeting suggests critical infrastructure pre-positioning.

incidents.victim: Asian organizations (technology, financial services, government)
incidents.vector: Multiple commercial AI LLMs (including Claude, Qwen, and DeepSeek) used to automate reconnaissance, vulnerability research, and attack planning in SecFlow-based offensive operations.
incidents.impact: Ongoing AI-assisted intrusion campaigns against Asian targets; documents operational use of multiple commercial AI systems to accelerate Chinese state-linked cyber operations.

incidents.victim: 70+ US companies (aerospace, energy, financial, healthcare, defense, cybersecurity)
incidents.vector: North Korean engineers used stolen identities and US-based laptop farm facilitators to secure remote IT employment; device identifiers spoofed and video capture cards used as fake webcams to evade detection.
incidents.impact: 14 indicted (2 arrested), 40+ laptop farms raided, 187 computers seized; approximately $3M in wages funneled to Pyongyang for weapons programs; scheme persists despite ongoing law enforcement pressure.

incidents.victim: Ahold Delhaize (Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Albert Heijn, Delhaize, Profi, Mega Image)
incidents.vector: Unknown attack vector; IT infrastructure supporting online ordering and distribution systems targeted, forcing precautionary shutdowns across multiple countries.
incidents.impact: Online orders, distribution operations, and in-store pricing disrupted across US, Netherlands, Belgium, and Romania; more than 400,000 employees and millions of customers affected.

incidents.victim: Ledger Nano X hardware wallet users (CryptoBilis reseller purchases)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — supply chain threat actor (alleged Chinese-linked company)
incidents.vector: Spy chips soldered inside Ledger Nano X wallets sold through a Southeast Asian reseller intercept seed phrases from the device screen and exfiltrate them via built-in eSIM modem to attacker infrastructure.
incidents.impact: $86 million in cryptocurrency stolen; Ledger advising customers to discard all affected devices and move funds immediately; isolated cases found in additional wallet models suggest broader supply chain exposure.

incidents.victim: FBI (employee intelligence data); Jeppesen ForeFlight / Boeing (aviation data)
incidents.vector: FBI employee data stolen via compromised credentials; Oracle PeopleSoft WAF bypass used in separate extortion attacks; stolen data leveraged to extort Boeing's aviation subsidiary Jeppesen ForeFlight.
incidents.impact: Sensitive FBI employee intelligence role data exposed; Boeing spin-off extorted; multiple ShinyHunters suspects arrested in Netherlands, US, and Jordan as law enforcement closes in on the group.

incidents.victim: OpenAI
incidents.vector: An OpenAI software engineer (Saudi national) installed a covert audio recording device inside the executive conference room to capture sensitive business and strategic discussions.
incidents.impact: OpenAI executive communications compromised over an unknown period; employee arrested by DOJ; extent of intelligence collected and potential foreign recipients under investigation.

incidents.victim: Foschini Group UK brands (Phase Eight, Hobbs, Whistles)
incidents.vector: Unknown attack vector; IT systems at TFG's three UK fashion brands disrupted, requiring partial system shutdowns.
incidents.impact: Multiple IT systems offline; online orders delayed; stores remained open; potential customer data exposure under investigation; second cyber incident involving TFG's UK operations this year.

incidents.victim: SkyNet ISP (St. Petersburg, Russia)
incidents.vector: Sustained DDoS attack combined with claimed network device disruption by Ukrainian hacktivist group BO Team since Oct 6, 2026; stated retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centers.
incidents.impact: Ongoing service disruptions affecting internet, VoIP, gaming, and video services for residential and business customers across St. Petersburg; more than 15,000 network devices claimed disabled; full recovery timeline unknown.

incidents.victim: Meta
incidents.vector: Employee credentials compromised and used to access Meta's internal GitHub repositories.
incidents.impact: Data of 1,500+ US employees stolen including sensitive role information; portions of Meta source code exfiltrated; employees being notified.

incidents.victim: Android phone buyers (cheap flagship-imitating models sold globally)
incidents.vector: Midnight Mimosa malware pre-installed at manufacturing or distribution stage on cheap Android phones mimicking flagship devices (S25 Ultra, i17 Pro); Google Play Store disabled by the malware to evade detection.
incidents.impact: Unknown number of users affected globally; malware enables clickjacking, proxy botnet participation, and ad fraud; Bitdefender research published; ongoing supply chain risk with no clear remediation path for affected devices.

incidents.victim: European grocery retailers (Intermarché and others — 400+ stores across France, Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany, Belgium)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of default credentials and outdated firmware in Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration controllers and XWEB management systems to remotely raise freezer and refrigerator temperatures to 50°C.
incidents.impact: 400+ French stores affected; tens of millions of euros in food stock destroyed; similar incidents reported across five additional European countries; Danfoss vulnerabilities had been publicly disclosed months before the attacks.

incidents.victim: Government, critical manufacturing, healthcare, and IT organizations globally
incidents.attacker: China — state-sponsored espionage group (Integrity Technology Group)
incidents.vector: AI-enabled automated scanning, large-scale botnets, and manual exploitation of internet-facing infrastructure; Integrity Tech provides tools, operators, and hosting to support Chinese state-directed cyber operations.
incidents.impact: Ongoing global campaign targeting critical sectors across multiple continents; joint advisory issued by UK, US, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Spain; Integrity Tech previously sanctioned by the UK government.
